s1.syndrome_frame: Unilateral ocular findings with facial angioma and increased intraocular pressure
salient_findings: Bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve
Iris heterochromia with diffuse hyperpigmentation and micronodular elevations on the iris surface in the right eye
Increased intraocular pressure in the right eye
key_facts: 12-year-old boy
Facial angioma
No leptomeningeal vascular malformations on MRI
Bilateral naevus flammeus
Visual acuity 20/20 in each eye
Iris heterochromia in the right eye
Intraocular pressure 22 mm Hg in the right eye and 12 mm Hg in the left
Open angles bilaterally
Diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye
Increased retinal vessel tortuosity in the right eye
Diffusely darker fundus in the right eye
Choroidal thickness 2.2 mm in the right eye and 1.4 mm in the left
Early visual-field defects in the right eye

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Facial angioma and unilateral ocular findings with increased intraocular pressure

shortlist.label: Glaucoma
shortlist.why_kept: Increased intraocular pressure in the right eye

shortlist.label: Phakomatosis pigmentovascularis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral naevus flammeus and ocular findings

shortlist.label: Diffuse choroidal hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Increased choroidal thickness and retinal vessel tortuosity in the right eye

shortlist.label: Ocular melanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Iris heterochromia and diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve, iris heterochromia, and increased intraocular pressure in the right eye are consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome.

rejected.label: Glaucoma
rejected.why: While increased intraocular pressure is present, it is not the primary diagnosis, but rather a complication of the underlying condition.

rejected.label: Phakomatosis pigmentovascularis
rejected.why: This condition is a rare disorder that combines features of naevus flammeus and pigmentary skin changes, but the primary features of the case are more consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome.

rejected.label: Diffuse choroidal hemangioma
rejected.why: The increased choroidal thickness and retinal vessel tortuosity could be suggestive of a choroidal hemangioma, but the presence of naevus flammeus and other systemic features point towards Sturge-Weber syndrome.

rejected.label: Ocular melanosis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by increased pigmentation of the ocular tissues, but the case features a more complex set of findings that are not fully explained by ocular melanosis alone.
